headline: Stocks extended a strong holiday-shortened week with a Black Friday tech rebound, but the macro backdrop got tighter: core PCE rose to a 3-year high of 3.3%, Q3 GDP was revised up to 4.3%, and jobless claims fell to 189k, so markets now see a December 9 Fed hike as nearly certain.
highlights: Inflation is moving further from the Fed's 2% goal. October core PCE, the Fed's preferred gauge, rose 3.3% y/y against a 3.2% forecast and 3.1% in September, its highest in about three years. Headline PCE was 3.8%, in line with forecasts. The dashboard's official data shows the same pattern: core CPI rose to 2.9% from 2.8% and headline CPI to 4.1% from 4.0%. After the PCE report, estimated odds of a 25 bp hike on December 9 reached 98.1%, from a target range of 3.75–4.00% (upper bound 4.00% on the dashboard).

Growth and jobs give the Fed little reason to wait. Q3 GDP was revised up to a 4.3% annualized pace from 3.4%, the fastest in three years. Initial jobless claims fell to 189k against 200k expected, tying the 2026 low, and October payrolls were +165k. Fed officials have been hawkish: last week's minutes showed almost all officials expect more hikes, Waller said a half-point hike should be considered, and Williams said no 'dramatic' move is needed. Treasury Secretary Bessent warned that overtightening could hurt the economy. The Fed's quiet period before the meeting starts Nov 28, so no Fed speakers are expected in the coming week.

Stocks rose for a third straight day in the half-day session. The Dow was up about 510 points (+1%), the S&P 500 +1.2% and the Nasdaq +1.7%, led by chips, Meta and Amazon. Before today, the Dow and S&P were each up about 5% for the week, the best week since April 2025. On the dashboard, 81.1% of stocks are up, no sector is down, and the bottom checklist scores 5/8: VIX is back below 25 at 23.81 and 63% of stocks are above their 50-day averages. Still, there has been no 90% up day since the Nov 19 90% down day. SPY (728.32) and QQQ (650.99) remain in bearish trends, below their sell levels of 741.33 and 669.60.

Rates and the dollar are working against the rally. The 10-year yield rose about 6.5 bp to roughly 4.93% today after hitting a 2½-month low near 4.80% on Thursday; the dashboard shows 4.91%. The dollar index is near 104.00, close to a 19-month high. UUP is the only bullish index ETF on the dashboard (29.72, sell level 29.78), and its 'Dollar reversing lower' checklist item is still off. FXE (100.98) and the bearish trends in GLD (334.40), SLV and GDX are consistent with a firm dollar, although gold rose more than 1.6% today.

Credit has not confirmed the bounce. High-yield spreads are 377 bps and 'volatile,' up 51 bps over 20 days, and HYG (76.61) is still bearish, below its 76.83 sell level. Rate-sensitive small caps are close to a test: IWM is at 273.79, just under its 276.06 sell level, in a bearish trend since September. Despite the 4.9% 10-year, the dashboard's defensive sectors stay bullish: XLU (43.73), XLP (92.68), XLV (184.20) and XLRE (44.14). XLF and XLC turned neutral today.

Oil is a second inflation risk. Brent settled 3.5% higher at $94.61 on Wednesday after Yemen's Houthis said they attacked Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery, and it was quoted at $96.33 on Nov 26. On the dashboard, energy trends have not followed: USO (137.77, sell level 142.44), XLE (61.67) and XOM, CVX, COP and EOG all remain bearish.

releases.read: Hotter than expected and the highest in about 3 years. This is the Fed's preferred gauge, and it essentially secures a December hike (about 98% priced).
In line with forecasts. The year-over-year rise reflects the trend building up, not one hot month.
In line, but nearly twice the Fed's 2% target, and September was revised higher.

A big upward revision driven by consumer spending and software investment. Gross domestic income grew 4.4%, which backs up the strength. It adds to the case for tighter policy. Third estimate due Dec 23.

Lower than expected, tying the 2026 low, though mostly because of seasonal adjustment (unadjusted claims rose about 16K). Continuing claims fell 95K to 1.70M in the week that the November jobs survey covered.
Turned back into expansion. Another sign that factory activity is holding up.

upcoming.event: Fed quiet period before the Dec 8–9 FOMC
upcoming.why: No Fed speakers until the decision. Data, especially Friday's payrolls, will drive rate pricing. Markets are debating whether hikes continue in January and March.
Prior 13.4. An early regional read on manufacturing with oil near $95 Brent.
Prior 55.5. A reading still well above 50, alongside 4.3% GDP, would support higher yields and a stronger dollar (UUP bullish). It matters for the bearish XLI and CAT trends.
Shows demand for labor before Friday's payrolls. A strong number would add to the hawkish case.
A rate-sensitive sector with the 10-year near 4.9%. Relevant to XLRE and HD.
The week includes Thanksgiving, so seasonal swings are likely. The last reading of 189K ties the year's low.
Prior 54.5. Watch the prices-paid detail for services inflation, the sticky part of core PCE at 3.3%.
Prior +165K and 4.1%. Considered the only release that could derail a December hike, and only if job losses are severe. It will matter for IWM at its 276.06 sell level and for HYG.
